[h1]It's cute but that's about it[/h1] This is not really a game I can recommend fully. It's got a certain charm to it but it's shallow as can be and features some of the very worst Roguelite elements possible. I play a lot of these games and I can tell fairly easily how they work and compare to each other, this one lands pretty far down the list unfortunately and I don't see it being very entertaining in the long run. For the price point however, it's not a big investment so if you feel drawn to it or strongly curios then just go ahead and try it out, you'll know if you like it or not within the refund period. I'll definitely be playing more of it every now and then and maybe my opinion will change but currently I'm fairly disappointed. [h3]Positives[/h3] [list] [*]Very nice aesthetics [*]Relaxing soundtrack [*]Not very challenging, nice game to relax with [*]Upgraded weapons are fun for the most part [*]Characters feel distinct and varied [/list] [h3]Mixed[/h3] [list] [*]Character pain sounds get annoying REALLY quickly (you can turn them off thankfully) [*]Some bosses attacks are borderline unavoidable with certain characters [*]Lots of content but most of it feels very same-ish or is linked to grindy unlocks [/list] [h3]Negatives[/h3] [list] [*]Everything is locked behind some quest or progress [*]Upgrades are boring stat increases [*]Way too visually busy [*]Balancing feels off, both in regards to your stats as well as enemies [*]Everything is up to RNG, especially frustrating when trying to upgrade weapons [/list]

[h1][b]被游戏名耽误的优秀类幸存者[/b][/h1] [h1]前言[/h1] 《暮光幸存者》除了这个游戏名不起眼外，无论是画面表现、技能设计、技能特效、爽快度等都有不错的表现，整体品质说是压过一众类幸存者游戏也不为过。 [h1]多样的角色设计[/h1] 一进入游戏，就能立刻感受到本作在画面与UI方面的精致，这两部分的表现相当成熟。 游戏设计了多个可用角色，无论是萝莉、忍者柴犬，还是机器人、榴莲宝宝，都做的十分精美，可爱的卡通画风一下子就能俘虏人的眼睛。 系统为每个角色均赋予了对应定位与玩法，除了数值上的不同外，角色们各自拥有一个专属技能，如柴犬的手里剑与冲刺杀敌、机器人的堡垒模式、榴莲的反伤玩法等。 每个角色还拥有一系列天赋升级，完成各类成就、在战斗中达成一些特殊进度、完成收集或解锁等内容时均会获得对应代币。 天赋能从重生次数、攻击力、移动速度、暴击率、经验获取、拾取范围、特殊技能等多个方向提升角色，但将所有角色升级分开的做法让这部分内容显得特别肝。 [h1]经典的生存模式[/h1] 游戏目前拥有翠绿草原、龙吟雪山、神圣沙漠、侵蚀之地等场景，这些场景下又划分了多个关卡，难度依次递升。 本作的游戏模式和《吸血鬼幸存者》类似，每个关卡中会源源不断的袭来敌人，玩家需要尽力生存，杀敌提升战力，最后迎接关底Boss的到来，这期间还要经历几波精英怪的攻击。 [h1]技能设计表现出色[/h1] 每升一级，玩家都可以从系统给出的三个技能中选择一个，这些技能设计的非常不错，虽然依然没有离开冲击波、连锁闪电、飞剑、激光等类型，但是其整体攻击范围、频率、特性都调校的刚刚好。 尤其是特效部分，本作的特效兼顾了视觉表现与清晰度，即使到了后期各技能成型，依然没有大部分同类游戏都会出现的特效遮挡视野问题。 本作的技能系统也沿用了《吸血鬼幸存者》的那套，输出技能和辅助技能各5个栏位，玩家必须要在众多的技能中细心搭配。 到了后期，各技能满级后，如果输出技能和辅助技能搭配得当的话，便会触发超级武器，此时技能会进一步升级，无论是整体威力还是特效都有新的展现，是用来冲击高难度的关键。 [h1]结语[/h1] 本作构建了一个迷人的世界，精美的卡通画风下有着不错的爽快度，售价方面更是交个朋友，而且还在不断更新。 体验下来，《暮光幸存者》各个方面都有不错的表现，综合起来整体品质可以在这个品类排到前排了。 [code]双语评测，认准我们： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]双语评测[/url] Make Chinese and English speaker feel at home： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]Bilingual Curator[/url][/code]

Only a solid pick if you've never played the genre before. Quality is fine and serviceable, but the gameplay feel leaves a lot to be desired. Specifically, the stages are too short to enjoy the feel of racking up power, and the power cap is too low to feel chaotic, and there's really awkward difficulty spikes that swap from 'nothing bad happens' to 'die in 1 second from offscreen'. The start is relatively grindy with the game requiring you to play the same character multiple times to unlock new powers, despite offering no meaningful gameplay changes. The primary downside is no level lasts more than 10~15 minutes at the beginning, and yet you're required to repeat those short loops too many times with no meaningful content changes.

I really enjoy this game and I typically like the survivor-like games. Disclaimer - This is my partner's review as she played the game through Steam Family Play.... I am not the type of player who enjoys Survivor games, and I don't remember ever even seeing one that really grabbed my interest. My partner has a tendency to enjoy making builds that let him stand in one spot, and that was always the turn-off of the series for me, if not for the titles that make their female character designs be too revealing/obvious what inspired their creation. Twilight Survivors changes up my view of the series with adorable art and landmarks on the maps that encourage you to travel around, even if you have a strong build. The shiba inu character is the first character I was introduced to and I immediately fell in love with his animations and little tail! After getting into the game and finding out they had specific quests to allow access to more character buffs, I also improved the game's outlook. The card system also intrigued me, being able to apply more buffs or even completely change how attacks work to create even more styles of play has been really fun to work with.

The premise of the game is good but it's all for nothing due to broken hit detection (your hitbox is twice as big as your character) and horrible balance. You'll find yourself playing a game until you get stuck in some level where you either have to grind for hours to get through or pray for a perfect rng, with no other way to get past. This game is genuinely a lot of fun and hits the mark for a “Survivor” style game. Naturally, people will want to compare it to Vampire Survivors, which is totally understandable. While Twilight Survivors has fewer heroes, each one is distinct, engaging, and rewarding to master—you’ll definitely want to try them all out. The graphics are surprisingly polished, and the game runs smoothly with just a slight hiccup when the screen fills up with enemies and effects. It’s a great choice if you’re looking for that Survivors gameplay vibe but with new environments and enemy types to keep things fresh. My only real gripe is with the card system—duplicates show up way too often, and since you can’t sell or recycle them, collecting Kwent cards can get frustrating. Overall, I’d recommend this to both newcomers and seasoned players alike. Rating: 8/10

[b]Oh, if only the main characters were Edward and Bella.[/b] Here we have another Vampire Survivors clone. What sets this one apart is its anime aesthetic and the inclusion of many levels and characters. The gameplay remains the same: survive on the map amidst hordes of enemies coming from all directions. I must praise the visual aspect of the game - everything is done very beautifully and almost magically. It's interesting and enjoyable to play. Unfortunately, there's not much else to praise. There are many characters, but only a couple are actually playable. The levels are numerous, requiring 15 minutes of survival each, but they barely differ from one another. The upgrades are weak and dull, and the dash/ability mechanics feel clunky. Overall, for its price, the game isn't bad. If you love the genre, it'll definitely appeal to you. But I'd still prefer the original—gameplay matters more here than graphics. I really enjoyed Twilight Survivors, yet another entry in the survivors-like, "bullet heaven" genre. Positives: - Excellent character design. The player characters in particular look fantastic, but the enemies are also cute and charming. - Vibrant, colorful environments and weapon effects. The game is visually delightful. - Different stages have different gimmicks to mix things up a bit. - Weapons can be powered-up in very satisfying ways. - Each character has a skill tree that can significantly improve their stats as well as boosting the abilities of their weapons and unique skills. - There is a surprising amount of lore, with several pages of character-specific story unlocked as you accomplish specific tasks for each character. Negatives: - Each weapon has another weapon or buff it pairs with to access a powered-up version of that weapon. This leads to focusing on specific pair-ups instead of experimenting with different playstyles. - Each character has a unique weapon no other character can use, which means that if you play like I did and focus on powering-up your weapons, there are certain buffs that will almost never be chosen because they only power up one character's weapon. For instance, I love being able to increase my pick-up range, but almost never used the Spatial Ring because it can only be combined with Emberfire's (the robot's) weapon. - Some of the weapons and buffs just seem severely underpowered. I never found a benefit to using minions (except for the health-restoring totems), and the buff to your dash distance doesn't really seem to do much at all. I had enough fun with Twilight Survivors that I stuck with it until I got all the achievements. It's true that a lot of these types of games tend to play quite similarly, but this game's visual identity goes a long way it making it feel unique. The wonderful character design was honestly a big motivator that kept me playing. Recommended.

This is a solid game. Very colorful, nice graphics without getting so overwhelming that you can't see or need a nasa level CPU to keep up. It is fun and for the price, you could and have probably done a lot worse. Several chars to unlock and play. However it is not always obvious on how the game works. At the heart of it, you have weapon cards to pick from, then skill cards to pick from. picking the right weapon and skill card together will evolve the weapon to super weapon status. Pretty standard right? Hmm maybe. You have to pay attention to the little icons on each type of card. You have to match them up and it can be confusing. You must reach super weapon status on at least half of your weapons in order to handle the bosses. If you don't you will get rolled. You can also unluck and equip upto 4 special cards between matches. These will mod the weapons you will use during the matches. Play to unluck more choices. There is not a ton of different weapons to use, but a few. Tho, you will probably want to stick with a select three or four on each run. Nothing new here for vets of these types of games, but nothing bad here either. 'Cept maybe the stages, lore, and skill enhancments being locked behind a progression system. This game can confuse, just pay attention to what you are reading in game and you will be fine. The game is enjoyable to play.

The heroes all have unique abilities so every run with a new hero has it's own experience. You can freely respec all your heroes so you can test all heroes. Got some cute Waifu baddies. 8/10

LMAO An easy recommend and in fact given the price point I encourage people to buy this game to support the developer and publisher because it's worth it.

REVIEWED AFTER BEING PLAYED ON: GeForce GT 1030/i7-3770 -Loving it so far! Probably one of the best games in the survivor genre out there. A must-get for fans of this particular gameplay style, be it on sale or not. The game pulled me in from the start, and did not want to stop playing it. Let's break it all in points of interest. ✨ PERFORMANCE: Game works beautifully and smooth for me. Even if the screen can get loaded with enemies, particles, and animations, the game did not lag once for me. ✨ PLAYABILITY AND FUN FACTOR: Like all survivor games, be ready to feel like you are grinding, farming, dodging, and surviving. And like all games in the genre, repetition is a need. The game will be repetitive a lot of times, but as you progress you will become attached to it and probably addicted. Characters each have their own set of talents to unlock and level up, each one with their own combat system. My fave so far is darling Lilia, even if I tried the other ones in the starter set before unlocking my first character. She's a melee character, but as you play you will have the chance to turn her into an AOE monster. There are also a lot of formulas and or combos you can implement in your runs depending on which ability cards you choose, you'll have fun experimenting with combinations and see what fits your style best. There are also a lot of events, hidden you could say. I randomly encountered some in the maps which gave me more options and made runs different. Every run is rewarding, and you will need hands with each character since the level of challenge depends on leveling up, mastering their skills, and learning from your falls. Don't expect the game to be an easy automatic walk in the park. Has a decent learning curve to master, but each character adds a level of uniqueness to it all. ✨ UNLOCKABLES: This game has a lot of content and stuff to unlock which makes it everlasting fun. You will unlock upgrades for your character skill trees, characters, multiple achievements, and interesting lore with rewards. This makes the game far more interesting compared to most titles in the genre, it's a matter of playing all characters and unlocking all the side content for each one. This of course, takes quite some time. That which you can balance freely on your own without frustrating yourself over senseless difficulties and endgame. ✨ EXCLUSIVE CONTENT: This game is as friendly as the developers behind it. The fact they are releasing updates with new characters, mechanics, modes, free DLC, acts or chapters, and reworking or enhancing the game casually, makes this a game worth supporting. Feels like an online experience somewhat you could say. Can't wait to see how far they take this project. 10/10: If you're a survivors/twin-stick shooter/bullet heaven game fan, then do get this one for your collection! Fun set of characters, clean animations, enemy variety, tough bosses, and unique runs to experience.

金玉其外，败絮其中，就是对这个游戏最准确的形容。单从卖相上看，本游戏可以称得上令人惊艳，你很难想象能用如此低廉的价格买到一款有着优秀的卡通建模、精致的攻击动画、完善的系统UI、甚至还有配音的幸存者游戏。然而，但你真正解锁了全部游戏内容之后，再来审视这整个游戏系统，你就会发现这真的是一款烂到令人难以置信的幸存者游戏，相较于吸血鬼幸存者非但没有任何拿得出手的创新可言，反而削减了大量内容，内核贫乏至极。 本游戏有多样化的武器吗？没错，是有的。然而所有角色的专属武器都不能被其他角色获取，只留下大量意义不明的角色专属被动来污染升级卡池。通用可进化的超级武器一共18件，其中有4件召唤武器，由于召唤物的伤害会独立于玩家单独计算，因此召唤系需要的实际加成有玩家+召唤物两套，加上召唤武器本身也偏弱，可以忽略。还有2件由两件武器组合而成的超级武器，其优势为不绑定特定技能而具有灵活的技能选择，但若不想亏损武器位的话，组合武器相当于会损失5个等级，而且在武器成功组合为超级武器之前不能通过商店/剑灵获取额外的武器，会严重拖慢前期的成长，因此即便这两件组合超级武器本身并不弱，也不建议选取。剩下的12件标准的超级武器中，还有多件如涌泉这样弱到令人发指的垃圾，综合来看值得一用的武器屈指可数。而更可怕的地方在于即便垃圾选项已经如此之多，而通关玩家手中居然有多达4个BAN位来应对这些问题，这可真是太充裕了。 本游戏有多样化的局外成长吗？没错，是有的，每个角色都有自己独有的技能树……然而，这个技能树存在的唯一意义就是让你点满它。没有分支选项，没有构筑抉择，甚至所有角色的后半段技能树都是相同的，提供的也仅有基础属性。更可怕的是解锁技能树所需的回忆，什么叫做完成回忆3所需满足的三个条件之一为通关"死亡之神的化身"，而完成回忆4所需满足的条件仅有通关"死亡之神的化身"？什么叫做维拉完成回忆3所需的条件之一是完成回忆5你告诉我？ 本游戏有个性化的强化内容吗？没错，是有的，本游戏有一个卡牌系统，其中包含了上百张效果各异的卡牌，可以从BOSS掉落的卡牌中三选一带走，并在通关时添加到卡牌库中。但数值设计上的问题先不说了，什么叫做三选一选的是暗牌？我是要选左边这张呢，还是右边这张呢，或者说是中间的呢，这可真是一个艰难的决定呢，毕竟我完全不知道它们是什么！所以我选不选究竟有什么区别你告诉我？ 总而言之，本游戏堪称教科书级别的样本，向你展示如何将众多优质的素材堆砌成为只为浪费玩家时间而存在的垃圾，并在所有的关键设计上与玩家的期望背道而驰。你以为后期可以解锁其他角色的专属武器，让那些越来越多的角色专属技能变得有用吗？错！你以为既然存在封印系统和越来越多的角色，那一定可以获取越来越多的BAN位来精简升级选项吗？错！你以为BOSS暗牌卡牌三选一一定是有意义的，后期可以将之变为明牌选择吗？错！你以为既然存在无尽模式，那一定可以给玩家带来全新的挑战吗？错！甚至为了完成维拉的回忆3、技能树都有一大半没解锁时就已经可以顺手打穿无尽模式了，剩下的只有差不多的任务、差不多的地图和差不多的敌人罢了。

一款大杂烩类幸存者游戏。画风本身挺可爱的，角色与怪物设计也有鲜明辨识度，整体UI包装做得很完整，第一眼会让人产生一种它应该挺好玩的期待。可真正开始玩后会发现它有一个合格的外壳，玩法却配不上这个外壳。其实游戏初期我还挺喜欢的，但是经过几次更新之后问题暴露得很明显。 先说优点。画风好看，声音反馈不错，音效在打击感和状态变化上体验挺好的，基础循环和构筑框架本身没有太大问题。局内成长、技能组合、刷怪推进，这套类幸存者游戏最基本的骨架是完整的。卡牌系统在我这是加分项，局内随机三选一让流程多了一些变化，部分卡牌设计也有巧思，很有意思。局外养成虽然资源需求略显膨胀，每一局给的货币太少了，但因为角色进度可以重置，某种意义上也缓和了养成压力，你不必真的把所有角色都硬养起来，这点多少算是给人留了余地。 这款游戏最明显的毛病，就是过于依赖堆怪来制造难度。屏幕被怪物塞满，数值一层层往上抬，视觉效果与伤害特效一起炸开，看上去确实热闹，甚至会给人一种紧张刺激的错觉，可实际上这种难度设计是很偷懒的。真正优秀的战斗压力，从来不只是把怪堆得更多，而是逼迫玩家持续作出决策层：究竟该拉怪还是切怪，该卡边缘游走还是留在中心输出，该冒险去吃经验还是稳妥保命，该提前站位还是临场闪避。换句话说，好的压力设计会不断要求你思考，而不是一味地堆叠，节奏控制能力明显不合格。 类幸存者游戏本来就很容易陷入后期大杂烩的陷阱，所以越是这种类型，越需要在节奏上做减法、做分层、做留白，而游戏后期关卡中，怪越来越多，画面越来越乱，角色被卷进一场数值洪流之中，所谓难度，并没有转化成策略密度，反而只剩下拥挤。角色强度的不平衡则进一步放大了这个问题。角色在设定上是有区别的，但这种区别并没有被妥善地平衡成不同风格，而是很明显的强度差距，我实在想不到要怎么用莉莉娅、犬影这类角色去通关擎天绘卷，我下载卸载了这款游戏好几次就是因为我打不过，在第二次更新的时候官方曾经削弱过那次更新的关卡的难度，说明他本身也知道难度曲线的不合理。这次总算是拿维拉，带蛮牛图腾+不要停下来+圣徽的护佑+亡灵大师平推了，但是感觉这是找最优解的作业而非体验构筑。 我玩这个明明是为了体验割草的不是吗，我为什么要在这做优解呀，类幸存者本应鼓励试验和组合快感，非优解很难过关而不应该是不能过关，把数值、怪量与关卡压力共同收束到少数解法时乐趣在哪呢，还有那个意义不明的破ban位设计，一个ban位就要五千货币，最后给四个ban位，可它本身对玩法改善到底有多大呢？与其说这是策略空间，不如说更像一种效率低下的资源消耗。

Note: game has not been updated since december 2024 and developers have not posted. this indicates to me that the game should be evaluated "as is," and this review emerges from that assumption. Twilight Survivors occupies an interesting place on the difficulty curve, as from the beginning it appears to be incredibly simple but it does develop nicely to a strong 'higher' difficulty near the end. The controls are more or less what you would expect in the genre, but some of the game-unique bindings are in locations I found odd--nothing I couldn't get used to. While the midgame space for build variation is pleasingly flexible, I found that the later I progressed, the more I had 'mandatory' skills and weapons for builds, and the variety became much subtler, if any remained at all. Part of this is due likely to my own playtime--This review is written post-completion, but only just. I haven't found out if there's a skill gap I can traverse to try something slightly wackier, and don't know that I will be in a hurry to do so as I have plenty other games to play... The character variety is strong, and I found I had my favorites which I would use to pass particular challenges even if I had no progress left to make on them. Others felt more like obligatory playthrough for the achievements + skill trees ('talent' trees in this game... more on that) was more than I wanted. The games were usually 10-15 minutes in length, with 12 feeling the most common to me. While there are freeplay modes, in most instances you will not have the option. The boss fight proceeds from the end of the clock but the length is not shown until after either you or the boss(es) die. The level scoring (D up to S) was fairly opaque to me, but I also found past a certain point, if I was beating a level I was getting an S grade anyway. the criteria (boss kill time, monsters killed, level achieved, coins collected) were straightforward enough, if a bit odd (coins collected feels strange to me, and boss kill time seems like it's a sufficient metric for the whole thing, no?) and rarely did my grade surprise me. What made playing Twilight Survivors fun was that unlike many other survivors games I have played, the community-provided strategy is relatively sparse. The temptation to follow suggestions is often too strong to resist, or can even feel necessary at times. Here, though, the opportunity to actually work on builds myself was refreshing, but if you find yourself relying upon strategy guides the dearth for this game may frustrate. The skill trees remain my only real sticking point. I did not feel as though the game was clear that some skill tree upgrades applied to all characters while others didn't. I'm still not entirely certain which ones do and don't, and it took me a while before I realized I just how much I had been limiting myself. This may be a me issue, but I'd rather a common skill tree plus individual skill trees so I don't need to keep resetting purchased levels as I hop between characters or figure out where my coins are best allocated. Because I hadn't realized this until later than I should have, I spent a stupid amount of money buying kwent cards out of the belief that simply swapping skills purchased as I swapped characters was enough trouble that I'd like the cards unlocked earlier... nope. Don't worry about buying more kwent cards until much later in the game, if at all. Most of the cards I found myself preferring came from quest rewards, anyway. Kwent cards are perhaps the 'most' unique (or least cookie-cutter) aspect of twilight survivors, and in that way I think they succeeded enough to make gameplay interesting, but I also couldn't really figure out if I liked the mechanic or not. Some levels you don't gain any and thus the only modifiers on your hero are ones you've selected, others you can acquire 10 or more. The randomness of the elite & boss-dropped cards was often infuriating, but that's the way she goes, I suppose. the "set" feature (equipping multiple specific cards to gain a greater ability) sounded nice but by the time I had any sets unlocked, the ones I could have used were far too weak to consider worth it. All in all, a solid entry into the genre. Nothing groundbreaking, but good variety, and at a good price. I don't think a sale is necessary ($3 is quite reasonable) but it's important to remember before you buy that the game almost certainly will not change from what it is now.
